stops.note: from coquere 'to cook' (Vulgar Latin cocina); the Roman cookbook attributed to Apicius is titled De re coquinaria, 'On cookery'
reached English through West Germanic (German Küche); in Anglo-Saxon monasteries the Rule of St Benedict rotated kitchen duty among the monks week by week
'kitchen sink drama' named the gritty British theatre of the 1950s, such as John Osborne's Look Back in Anger (1956)

current_meaning: a room where food is prepared and cooked
